title: The pack, its three check codes, the two operations, the five schemas, the parameter rows, the decided-version rule and the record code are not in the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-014); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.25); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.1, T3.2, T-A); _work/msr/context/P4.md (ownership rows, Architecture v5 slide 14)
description: No source defines what a pack is for this service, the three checks it must pass, the two operations that carry the check and its read, the field set of a pack row or a defect item, the parameter rows the check depends on, the rule that a decided pack version is never decided twice, or the decision-record code a verdict is written under.
evidence: RWB-E8-014 gives one story sentence, two generic criteria, four test cases and a data table of assignment, decision_log_entry, rule_row and role, and its endpoints are POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions and its approve, which belong to RWB-P4-AD011-APP and RWB-P4-AD012-APP; FSD P4 v3 A2.25 gives the intent, the metric, the three generic steps, the prerequisite FEAT-LIT-05, the validation rule VR-P4-025-1 and BR-P4-025, and no operation, no field and no state; TSD P4 v3 T-A declares API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none of them is a pack check, and T5.3 states the events of P4 as None; the context pack lists the four P4 REST operations provided (GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants) and none is a pack operation; Architecture v5 slide 14 names the P4 contract as authorise, me/permissions, doa-limits and masking-policies.
proposed: Fix the pack as a candidate version of this service's own access model with PERMISSION, SCOPE and MASKING rows and the two operations POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/pack-checks and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/pack-checks; fix the three check codes PC-ENT, PC-SCP and PC-MSK over role, permission and masking_rule, the verdict set ACCEPTED and RETURNED, the decided-version 409, the parameter rows access.pack.personalAreas, access.pack.rowLimit and the page bounds read through DP-06, and the verdict entry of the DP-03 chain; leave the load and the approval of a matrix version to RWB-P4-AD002-APP and the screen to RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

title: The feature specification makes the check an unattended batch or event step and its only validation rule an ACE data-freshness rule, while the key carries no DP-05 and no DP-10
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.25.2, A2.25.3.1, A2.25.4.4); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (patterns of RWB-E8-014: DP03, DP06, DP13, DP19); _work/msr/context/P4.md (DP table, ownership rows); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-014)
description: FSD P4 v3 A2.25.2 makes the step run unattended on a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer, and A2.25.3.1 gives VR-P4-025-1, a data-product staleness rule over v_ace_batch_status with MSG-P1-001 naming a data product; A2.25.4.4 declares no background event. The key's pattern list carries neither DP-05 nor DP-10, so the slice can read no ACE view and can own no Temporal Schedule, and the context pack gives the service no event to consume.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.25.2 step 1 reads 'Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer', A2.25.3.1 row VR-P4-025-1 reads 'Data product stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source (v_ace_batch_status)' with MSG-P1-001, and A2.25.4.4 reads 'None | No background event'; split_plan.json fixes the patterns as DP03, DP06, DP13 and DP19 and none is DP-05 or DP-10; the context pack lists the P4 events as None and the jobs as JOB-18 only, and DP-05 and DP-10 each add a platform dependency the metadata does not carry; TSD P4 v3 T5.2 keeps P4's ACE contact to the published interfaces and T5.3 declares no event.
proposed: Read the trigger as the submission of a pack through the administration screen: the check is request-driven, starts no workflow and owns no Schedule, and the task a person needs is the returned-packs list of SCR-39. Leave the freshness of an ACE data product to rwb-source-data and its own contract, and do not implement VR-P4-025-1 in rwb-access.

title: Two sources disagree on who submits a pack and who reads it, and the legacy permission table's approve letter has no leg in this key
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-014 Permission checks); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T6.1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.25.3.3)
description: The legacy story's permission table gives Rules and parameters C to RW-COE and Rules and parameters A to RW-RISK, and its endpoints are a rule-version load and its approve; the story's persona is a litigation officer, and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-LITOFF R in Rules and parameters and a dash in platform administration. The key has no approval leg, so the A letter has no object here, and no source says which role submits the check and which role reads the returned pack.
evidence: RWB-E8-014 Permission checks reads 'Rules and parameters | C | RW-COE' and 'Rules and parameters | A | RW-RISK'; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 reads 'RW-LITOFF Litigation officer | R | R | -' and 'RW-COE Center of excellence analyst | CRUD | CRUD | R'; FSD P4 v3 A2.25.3.3 reads 'None; runs unattended | Primary' and 'Litigation officer | Also uses'; RWB-E8-014 carries two criteria and no approval step, and its data table carries no matrix or masking row.
proposed: Fix the submit as Rules and parameters C, held by RW-COE, and the read as Rules and parameters R, held by the owner role the pack is returned to (RW-LITOFF and RW-AUDIT), and keep no approve leg in this key: the approval of a matrix version belongs to the administration stories of this service. Confirm the split with the security administrator before the operations are frozen.

title: The wording of MSG-GEN-002 and MSG-GEN-004 and of the defect items is not in any source read for this work package
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-014 Validation and messages); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md
description: MSG-GEN-002 (a value outside its range) and MSG-GEN-004 (a record that moved or was decided) are used as identifiers by other stories of the run, but no source in this read set gives their wording, and no source gives the wording of a defect item, which is a new element of this contract.
evidence: RWB-E8-014 Validation and messages lists MSG-P4-004, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-001, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003 and no MSG-GEN-002 or MSG-GEN-004; the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 extract carries VR-P4-025-1 and BR-P4-025 and no message catalogue; the acceptance criteria of other modules cite MSG-GEN-002 as 'value outside its range' and MSG-GEN-004 as a refused second change without quoting either text.
proposed: Carry MSG-GEN-002 and MSG-GEN-004 by identifier with their text marked not specified, and let the message catalogue supply both before the operations are frozen; keep a defect item free of a message ID, because a defect names the row, the field and the rule and is not a catalogue message.
